newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones leaps to second biggest daily gain ever.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones leaps to second biggest daily gain ever.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average racked up its second biggest one-day gain ever Tuesday, boosted by positive news on retail inflation and a batch of solid corporate earnings.

The world's most closely watched stock index ended with a gain of 135.26 points, or 2.10 percent, at 6,587.16 -- the next best gain in point terms after soaring 187 points on Oct. 21, 1987, or two days after the "Black Monday" crash that wiped out 508 points from the Dow.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,840 to 764 on active volume of 506 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The 30-stock Dow index has been on the comeback trail since Monday, when it jumped 60 points, and has erased more than a quarter of the nearly 700-point decline it posted after setting its last record high close of 7,085.16 on March 11.
Investors were relieved that the Consumer Price Index for March did not confirm the inflationary pressures suggested in Friday's Producer Price Index report.
The inflation report had kept investors on edge, particularly in light of a 148-point sell-off in the Dow last Friday on the unexpected 0.4 percent rise in wholesale prices.
"It's a sigh of relief that our worst fears were not materialised," said John Church, chief investment officer at the Glenmede Trust Co.

The Labour Department said the CPI rose 0.1 percent in March, after rising 0.3 percent in February. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the index rose only 0.2 percent after being up the same amount in February.
The bond market also was buoyed by Tuesday's inflation data. The Treasury's 30-year bond gained nearly a full point, and its yield tumbled to 7.09 percent from Monday's close of 7.17 percent.
Strong earnings from Dow components Caterpillar Inc. and Eastman Kodak Co. were both among the companies reporting earnings that exceeded Wall Street estimates.
"My argument has been that strong earnings should provide the antidote for this market," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "So far they are."
Caterpillar rose 3-5/8 to 83 and Kodak gained 2-1/8 to 75-1/4.
There were weak spots in the market, however, most notably technology stocks.

Intel Corp. tumbled 2-3/4 to 131, one day after warning that its revenue growth was likely to slow in coming quarters. The comments overshadowed the company's strong first quarter results reported Monday and cast a pall over the technology group.

A second blow came as Salomon Brothers trimmed its earnings estimates on networking bellwether Cisco Systems Inc. Salomon cited product transitions and general industry sluggishness as representing significant challenges for Cisco, which slid 3-1/8 to 50-1/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, fell 3.53 points to 1,212.88.
Analysts said the malaise in technolody stocks was symptomatic of a market still reluctant to engage in the widespread buying that marked the bull run of the last two years.

"When you're in a period of rising rates and changing monetary policy, people tend to look closer at the negatives," said Barbara Marcin, vice president at Citibank Global Asset Management. "It's not like a year ago, when people were able to ignore bad news."

Among individual issues, Avant! Corp. sank 12 to 12-1/2 after the Santa Clara County, Calif. district attorney's office said it filed felony charges against the company and several of its senior officials for allegedly stealing Cadence Design Systems Inc. technology.
The two companies make software that helps engineers design computer chips and have been bitter rivals. Cadence Design fell 1/2 to 30-1/2.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 10.99 points to 754.72. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.09 to 555.06.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 6.13 to 397.62. The average share was up 61 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,185.502 up 87.97 or 1.24 percent.
